collection.description: A friend proudly gives a villager a lumpy carved bowl with a turtle on it that is not much like a turtle.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (friend) has carved (subject) a bowl, and (friend.he/she) is so proud of it. It's lumpy. It's lopsided. It has a face on the side that (friend) says is a turtle and (subject) is fairly sure is not a turtle. (friend) is watching (subject.him/her) expectantly.

a__fx.name: Answer A
a__fx.text: "You made this for me?" says (subject). "Thank you." And (subject.he/she) means it, which surprises (subject.him/her) a little. (subject.He/She) uses the bowl for fruit, and every time (subject.he/she) looks at the not-quite-turtle, (subject.he/she) thinks of (friend) carving it with (friend.his/her) tongue sticking out. After a while the bowl stops looking lopsided and just looks like (friend).

b__fx.name: Answer B
b__fx.text: "Tell me about the turtle," says (subject). (friend) explains that it's a turtle who has just heard a very funny joke. (subject) looks again. It's still not much like a turtle. But now that (subject.he/she) knows about the joke, (subject.he/she) can see it perfectly: a creature that's about to laugh. (subject.He/She) puts it in pride of place.
